title: Load jobs from a config file
description: Adds `schedule.config.load_jobs(text, allowed, scheduler=None)`, so operators can list jobs in a text file in the same words as the Python API, one per line, for example `every monday at 09:00 do tasks.reports:weekly tags reports,mail` or `every 5 to 10 seconds do tasks.queue:poll`. Blank lines and `#` comments are skipped. The config file is edited by operators, not developers, so it can only reach code the application chose: the module must be one of `allowed` or a submodule of one, and the function must be defined in that module (not imported into it) and must not start with an underscore. Any invalid line raises `ScheduleValueError` whose message starts with `line <n>:`, numbered as an editor numbers lines, and then no job from the text is scheduled. Jobs go to `scheduler`, or to the default scheduler when it is None. Includes tests.

defects.summary: The function name pattern accepts a leading underscore, so a config line can schedule a module's private helpers.
A module is allowed when its name merely starts with an allowed name, so allowing "tasks" also allows "tasks_admin" or "tasksx".
defects.corrected: return any(module == name or module.startswith(name + ".") for name in allowed)
defects.defective: return any(module.startswith(name) for name in allowed)

defects.summary: Any callable attribute of an allowed module is accepted, including functions it imported (shutil.rmtree, os.system), not only functions defined there.
defects.corrected: if not callable(func) or getattr(func, "__module__", None) != module:

defects.summary: Each job is added to the scheduler as soon as its line is read, so when a later line is invalid the jobs before it stay scheduled.
defects.corrected:
entries.append((job, func))
    return [job.do(func) for job, func in entries]

defects.summary: Lines are numbered from 0, so every error names the line before the one that is wrong.

ceiling.summary: A zero interval is accepted, and schedule's Job._schedule_next_run then adds a zero period forever, so one config line such as 'every 0 seconds do ...' hangs load_jobs and the application.

decoys.why: The module name comes from the config text, but it is imported only after _allowed() has accepted it.
unit has already been checked against _UNITS, so getattr can only reach the unit properties.
